submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on hard-news wire-report prose (violence, crime, conflict, government/official actors, weekday datelines, 'officials/spokesman/police said' attribution), with activation building through the news sentence and peaking at the end of an attributed news sentence: on 'said'/the attribution phrase, the closing period, and above all the newline token that ends that paragraph (about 0.6-1.0 of max). Casual, personal, code or math text stays near 0; a mundane sentence ending in '..., X said.' followed by a newline gets only a weak floor (~0.2-0.3), and removing the trailing newline or ending with ':' instead of '.' drops the peak by about 0.2.
